newsitem.title: UK: UK inflation would overshoot without hike - Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK inflation would overshoot without hike - Brown.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said inflation would exceed the government target of 2.5 percent or less next year without corrective action in the form of higher interest rates.
"My judgment is that we have inherited a situation in which, in the absence of corrective action, inflation will overshoot the government's inflation target next year," he told a news conference.

He cited recent rapid growth in consumer spending, house price rises of six to nince percent a year, the recent pickup in average earnings and broad money supply growth as reasons for raising interest rates to 6.25 percent from 6.0 percent.

Against these inflationary pressures, Brown said he had had to weigh the strength of sterling, especially against the deutschemark, subdued producer price inflation, disappointing manufacturing activity, the weakneess of industrial investment and reduced optimism about export prospects.
He said no-one should doubt his determination to create conditions in which business and manufacturing could flourish.
